name: Darlington common-emitter voltage amplifier
description: Q1 and Q2 share a collector load and form a Darlington common-emitter stage. Q1 supplies Q2’s base current, increasing input resistance; R3 provides a discharge and bias path at the intermediate base. R1/R2 establish input bias, while R4 stabilizes DC emitter current and C2 bypasses it at signal frequencies. R5 sets collector loading, C1/C3 block DC, and R6/C4 represent a 10 kΩ load with 100 pF capacitance. At 12 V and 27°C, ngspice 46 gives 40.30 dB gain at 1 kHz, 207.0 mV peak-to-peak output for a 2 mV peak-to-peak input and 0.953 mA supply current. Open the saved Functional verification experiment to reproduce AC and transient results. ANPN is a generic educational model; device spread, tolerances and process corners are not qualified.
